Find the area bounded between the curve $y=\sqrt[3]{x-1}+1,$ the $y$-axis and the lines $y=0$ and $y=1,$ as shown above.

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we make $x$ the subject:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1) \\ {e}^{y} & =x+1 \\ x & ={e}^{y}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{y}-1)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={e}^{y}\,{|}_{0}^{1}-y\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(e-1)-(1-0) \\  & =e-1-1 \\  & =e-2\end{aligned}
$$
